eval_rubric:
1. The deck opens on the prospect's problem, not on us -- product and capabilities appear only after the pain is established, and the register throughout is persuasive, not a flat report.
2. A persuasive arc is present: cost of staying put follows the problem, proof and pricing come before the ask, and the ask closes the deck. Any reasonable slide breakdown and titles are acceptable -- grade the presence and relative ordering of these beats, not an exact structure.
3. Cost of inaction is derived from the stated pain (2% QA coverage, compliance exposure, 10-week ramp, supervisors scoring instead of coaching) and is framed sharply but NOT quantified with invented dollar figures.
4. The proof slide uses only the given stats (~3% -> 100% QA coverage, 40% less after-call work, ~one-third faster ramp), attributed exactly as given ('a comparable telecom'). No invented customer names, logos, or ROI numbers.
5. Pricing matches the brief ($45 / $90 / Custom per agent per month), and the ask lands the 60-day pilot on ~300 agents with the stated success criteria, framed as de-risking versus their stalled in-house build.
